ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, counterparties and escrow beneficiaries against: (i) United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List and UNSC resolutions implemented under the Sanctions Act 2018; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade consolidated sanctions registers; (iv) PEP databases and domestic and international adverse media sources; (v) FATF call-for-action lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, state-owned shipping counterparty, or jurisdiction with deficient AML/CFT regime; clear screening results and source of funds evidence must be recorded under AML/CFT Act 2009 sections 22-31.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online registry and NZBN company name availability system (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin-script English characters; Te Reo Māori words and diacritics are permitted but must be transliterated into plain Latin characters where necessary for the statutory register; names must be displayable in the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register and may not consist exclusively of symbols, punctuation or non-transliterable characters; foreign-language names must be accompanied by a certified English transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration to the New Zealand Registrar of Companies, supported by a statutory declaration, evidence of availability, and any ministerial/regulatory consent letters for sensitive tokens. The request must be lodged within 20 working days of the rejection notice. The Registrar will issue a formal review decision within 20 working days. A further refusal may be appealed by way of originating application to the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Act 2019 and Companies Act 1993, and the applicant should simultaneously reserve a corrected proposed name for immediate re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or agent-provided registered office is permissible only if a licensed registered-office service provider maintains a genuine physical street address in New Zealand, accepts service of process, maintains physical or accessible electronic records, and is not a PO Box-only arrangement. For an International Company engaged in ISIC 5222 offshore towage and salvage, the AML/CFT medium-risk enhanced rating means that functional operational substance -- a capable board, bank account, disbursement and escrow governance, voyage/charter management records, and salvor engagement protocols -- must be demonstrable; a mailbox-only virtual office is not acceptable for Maritime NZ licensing and tax substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% per annum (medium-high) for an offshore towage and salvage International Company, due to mandatory Maritime New Zealand marine safety and pollution-prevention inspection powers, AML/CFT supervision by the Financial Markets Authority, and the elevated risk profile of emergency salvage contracts; unannounced physical inspections are statistically probable within the first two operating years.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), Part 2 (Registration of Companies, ss 10-27), ss 13-15 (application, registration and certificate of incorporation), ss 28-41 (constitution), s 53 (return of allotments), ss 128-131 (issue and allotment of shares), ss 152-154 (composition of board and foreign-resident directors), ss 189-191 (registered office and address for service), together with the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2012.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), administered by the Registrar of Companies; the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register is operated as part of the same registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (online electronic form filed under s 13 of the Companies Act 1993 through the New Zealand Companies Office portal using a RealMe login; upon approval the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and assigns the NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under the Companies Act 1993; shares may be issued at no par value and for such consideration, including offshore foreign currency consideration, as the directors determine under s 128. No escrow, capital deposit or reserved account is required by the Companies Office; paid-up capital may be subscribed entirely offshore by non-resident shareholders subject to standard AML/CTF verification at the accepting New Zealand financial institution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the Company). At a first meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company duly convened and held on [date] at the registered office of the Company at [physical New Zealand address], the following resolutions were considered and, being passed by the unanimous consent of all directors entitled to vote, were adopted as resolutions of the Board: 1. Incumbency and Constitution: THAT the incorporation of the Company as an International Company under the Companies Act 1993, as evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), be and is hereby ratified, approved and confirmed; and THAT the constitution tabled before the Board be and is hereby adopted as the constitution of the Company with full force and effect in accordance with ss 28-31 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. Subscription and Allotment of Share Capital: THAT the issue of the authorised share capital, comprising [X] ordinary shares of no par value, together with any preference or management shares as may be authorised, be and is hereby approved; THAT the directors be and they are hereby authorised to allot and issue such shares to the persons named in the allotment schedule at such consideration as the directors determine, which consideration may be paid in cash, by set-off of lawful consideration, or in offshore foreign currency, and shall be duly recorded in the books and share register of the Company; and THAT a Return of Allotment be filed with the Registrar of Companies within the statutory period. 3. Registered Office and Address for Service: THAT the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [physical address, New Zealand], which office shall be open to the public at statutory hours, and THAT the Registrar of Companies and the NZBN register be notified of the registered office and the address for service in accordance with ss 189-191 of the Companies Act 1993. 4. Appointment of Officers: THAT the following persons be and are hereby appointed as officers of the Company: [Name] as Managing Director; [Name] as the New Zealand-resident director (or, where compliant with s 152 of the Companies Act 1993, an Australian-resident director); and [Name] as Company Secretary (optional), each to hold office upon the terms of the constitution and the Companies Act 1993, and each to be vested with authority to sign banking mandates, licence applications, employment and towage/salvage contracts, and statutory returns on behalf of the Company. 5. Banking and Payment Rails: THAT the opening of corporate current and escrow accounts in New Zealand be and is hereby authorised, and THAT all incoming and outgoing funds, including Lloyd's Standard Form wire transfers and escrow settlements, be accepted and disbursed solely in accordance with the Company's AML/CTF policies and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. 6. Licensing and Regulatory Compliance: THAT the directors be and they are hereby directed to procure all industrial, maritime and environmental licences necessary for the business of deep-sea tugboat towage and maritime emergency salvage, including the Maritime Operator Safety System (MOSS) certificate, New Zealand ship registration, Marine Protection Rules compliance certification, and any coastal shipping licence if domestic coastal trade is subsequently undertaken, and to maintain at all times the requisite insurance, including P&I, salvage liability and marine pollution cover. 7. Indemnification and Authority: THAT the directors and officers be entitled to the benefit of such indemnities and director and officer insurance as are authorised by the constitution, and THAT this resolution may be executed in counterparts and recorded in written minutes adopted by the Board.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand; digital portal: myIR at https://ind.ird.govt.nz; supplementary customs portal for physical export declarations: New Zealand Customs Service / Trade Single Window; business registration registry: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign offshore entity must first determine whether it has New Zealand source income or carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand. If no New Zealand source income and no fixed establishment, no compulsory IRD number is required; the entity may nevertheless obtain an IRD number for treaty identity or banking purposes using the applicable non-resident company registration application. If income tax registration is required, the non-resident company applies for an IRD number through myIR or by paper application, providing certified incorporation documents, director/shareholder identification, registered office details, and appointment of a New Zealand agent for service. For GST, the same IRD number serves as the GST registration number; the entity must file a GST registration application if taxable supplies in New Zealand are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period, or if voluntary registration is desired. The New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) may be obtained through the Companies Office and used for government and banking identification, but the NZBN is not a substitute for the IRD number. International Company (IC) status in the tax-exempt zone is preserved as long as the entity does not carry on activities creating New Zealand source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The CK_IC International Company is treated as a non-resident offshore entity for New Zealand tax purposes. It is not a pass-through vehicle; it is a limited liability taxable entity in principle, but its active foreign-source income from offshore towage and maritime salvage is outside the New Zealand income tax net provided no fixed establishment exists in New Zealand and the services are not sourced in New Zealand. Entity-level taxation of any New Zealand-source income would apply only if the IC carries on activities through a permanent establishment or derives income from New Zealand land, natural resources, or other New Zealand-source assets.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; classification follows the legal form and source rules. Relevant statutory elections available to a qualifying offshore company and its New Zealand group counterpart include: voluntary GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; election between invoice basis, payments basis, or hybrid basis for GST accounting; GST group registration election; consolidated group treatment for wholly owned New Zealand-resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2007 Part IS; provisional tax estimation method election; and approved issuer levy election for certain cross-border interest. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act 2007 are mandatory and cannot be broadly elected out, although limited exemption elections are available in prescribed mismatch structures. No check-the-box election is available to convert an International Company into a disregarded entity for New Zealand tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: New Zealand Goods and Services Tax (GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period; registration is compulsory once that threshold is exceeded, voluntary below the threshold; non-resident offshore supplies that are zero-rated under section 11B of the GST Act 1985 do not count toward the threshold unless supplied through a New Zealand fixed establishment or connected with New Zealand goods/land. Separate registration and GST return obligations apply to offshore suppliers of low-value imported goods under the GST Act 1985.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime is in force in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the Peppol network; IRD does not pre-clear invoices. GST-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices meeting section 24 of the GST Act 1985, using their IRD/GST number, supplier and recipient identification, taxable supply description, time of supply, GST rate, and amount. For zero-rated export services, the tax invoice should state the zero-rating basis, e.g., 'Section 11B, GST Act 1985'. Invoices may be transmitted electronically through EDI, email, PDF, or Peppol, and the underlying records must be retrievable for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Offshore towage and maritime emergency salvage services are eligible for zero-rating under section 11B of the GST Act 1985 when the recipient is a non-resident of New Zealand and is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and the services are not supplied directly in connection with land in New Zealand or moveable goods physically present in New Zealand. For deep-sea tugboat towage and salvage contracts concluded with non-resident shipowners, hull underwriters, Protection and Indemnity clubs, or Lloyds salvage arbitrators, the underlying vessel, cargo, and casualty site are located outside New Zealand territorial waters; the supply is therefore zero-rated. Services physically performed inside New Zealand, coastal towage of New Zealand goods, services to a recipient present in New Zealand, or services connected with New Zealand land are standard-rated at 15%. GST-registered exporters may claim input tax credits against zero-rated income and receive a refund from IRD where net GST is negative, subject to IRD verification of the shipment or service export evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Export Entry through Customs Trade Single Window) for any physical export component, e.g., towed vessels, equipment, or spare parts; not applicable to pure offshore service supplies
Bill of Lading or sea waybill covering any towed vessel or physical equipment; otherwise towage statement of facts / handover protocol
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 bank credit advice / escrow release statement evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident
Lloyd's Open Form (LOF) or executed marine salvage/towage contract identifying the non-resident principal and casualty location
Salvage master's statement of facts, tow logs, GPS/AIS tracking data, incident report, and classification survey
GST tax invoice satisfying section 24 of the GST Act 1985 with a narrative stating zero-rating under section 11B
Recipient non-resident certificate, corporate registry extract, and AML/KYC pack obtained through the escrow bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD audit scrutiny focuses on the non-resident status of the recipient, the physical location of salvage services, the absence of New Zealand fixed establishment, and the adequacy of contemporaneous documentation. If zero-rating is found to be incorrectly claimed, the supply is reassessed at 15% GST, with use-of-money interest running from the GST return due date. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 may be imposed at 20% for lack of reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness or an abusive tax position, and up to 150% for evasion or similar conduct. Criminal prosecution may be brought for knowingly filing false GST returns. GST refunds are subject to reassessment for seven years; a retrospective clawback will include unpaid tax, late payment interest, penalties, and, in cases of fraudulent export zero-rating claims for offshore towage salvage, liability for prosecution and disqualification of the responsible corporate officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) is the central bank and prudential supervisor of registered banks under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989; the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervises market conduct and non-bank financial institutions; the anti-money-laundering and countering-financing-of-terrorism (AML/CFT) regime is set out in the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and is enforced for registered banks by the Reserve Bank, for financial advice and non-bank lending licensees by the FMA, and for money-service businesses, money remitters, and high-value dealers by the Department of Internal Affairs. New Zealand maintains no exchange-control bureaucracy: there is no central-bank permit requirement for foreign-exchange conversion, no surrender-of-export-proceeds regime, and no designated FX rationing; all inward and outward payments are subject only to standard AML/CFT reporting, tax-declaration obligations, and, for foreign investments, the Overseas Investment Act 2005 where the underlying asset constitutes sensitive land or significant business assets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has a fully convertible currency in both the current and capital accounts. NZD/USD and NZD cross-rates are freely determined on a spot T+2 basis, and the Reserve Bank does not impose convertibility ceilings, capital repatriation controls, or prior approval for ordinary operating and treasury flows. New Zealand is an IMF Article VIII member, therefore international payments and transfers are unrestricted. Profit remittance from an International Company is constrained not by foreign-exchange convertibility but by non-resident withholding tax (NRWT): under the Income Tax Act 2007, dividends and interest paid to non-residents are subject to NRWT at a 30% default rate (or a lower income-treaty rate, e.g., 15% under the New Zealand-Australia double-tax agreement), unless the dividend is fully imputed or an exemption applies. For a tax-exempt International Company structure, remittance is best executed as a non-taxable return of capital or exempt intercompany distribution, supported by a formal board declaration and a capital-maintenance solvency statement under the Companies Act 1993, and, where prudent, an Inland Revenue ruling confirming the exemption. No separate profit-remittance tax or foreign-exchange approval exists under New Zealand law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand does not require exporters or cross-border service providers to surrender, convert, repatriate, or process export proceeds; there is no statutory timeline (such as the 90-day or 180-day surrender regimes common in other jurisdictions) and no mandatory conversion ratio. A maritime towage and salvage enterprise may retain 100% of Lloyd's Open Form awards, hire, and disbursement recoveries in USD or any foreign currency, whether held offshore or onshore. The only obligations are indirect: (i) banks report cross-border current and capital-account transactions to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand for balance-of-payments statistics; (ii) the AML/CFT Act requires prescribed transaction reporting for physical cash and international wires above NZD 10,000, and suspicious transaction reports without threshold; and (iii) tax legislation may require attribution and reporting of foreign currency balances where the entity is New Zealand tax-resident. Treasury should not contract any NZD conversion or liquidation of export proceeds; USD operating accounts and offshore escrow are fully compatible with this zero-surrender regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as an ancillary payment channel; Low as a standalone treasury or custody bank. Offshore digital EMI platforms, including cross-border business neo-banks such as Airwallex, Wise Business, Currenxie, and Revolut Business, are not licensed as registered banks in New Zealand under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. They cannot accept New Zealand call deposits, issue escrow letters, issue or confirm documentary letters of credit for maritime supply, or provide clearing guarantees. Such EMIs may offer remittance, multi-currency wallets, and card issuance only through an NZ-registered money-service business or a tier-1 bank sponsorship, and every such arrangement must satisfy New Zealand AML/CFT registration. The blueprint therefore treats EMIs as an optimisation layer for low-value operating suppliers in APAC corridors only, with a hard cap of 10% of monthly treasury flow and no overdraft, hedging, or escrow role.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the AML/CFT Act, corporate verification may in principle be completed electronically where the bank's electronic identity-verification process meets the statutory standard; however, in practice all major New Zealand banks combine remote verification with a synchronised video onboarding call. For a tax-exempt International Company with non-resident beneficial owners, banks typically require: (1) a recorded video interview with each beneficial owner and at least two authorised signatories; (2) original or notarially certified corporate registers, certificate of incorporation, and certificate of good standing, apostilled and where necessary legalised; and (3) in-person identity verification at a New Zealand branch or through a reputable foreign bank, notary, or embassy for the passport signature page. Some banks accept a remote opening path where an NZ-resident director, treasury manager, or licensed corporate-services provider already has an existing relationship; however, the marine-salvage use case, characterised by rapid emergency wires and high-value Lloyd's Standard Form settlements, triggers enhanced due diligence and may require a directors' session at the bank's Auckland Corporate Centre. The onboarding calendar should allow 15 business days, with contingency for in-person attendance by the Managing Director and one independent director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt 'International Company' classification interpreted by underwriters as potential tax evasion or shell-company red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation and company constitution; deemed-exempt or tax-exemption confirmation from Inland Revenue New Zealand; New Zealand registered-office agreement and licensed corporate-services-provider engagement letter; audited financial statements reflecting maritime operating substance; OECD CRS and GAAR reporting confirmations; board-pack explaining commercial purpose of towage and salvage contracts; and a group structure chart with full beneficial-ownership mapping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse sanctions or politically-exposed-persons (PEP) flags arising from vessel operators, charterers, insurers, or beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial-ownership chain mapped from the statutory register; sanctions screening results against OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated List, UN Security Council, New Zealand Autonomous Sanctions Regulations, and HM Treasury; vessel IMO registration and flag-state extracts; Equasis and Lloyd's Register safety records; maritime counsel sanctions clearances for each voyage; and a board-approved no-engagement-with-sanctioned-vessels policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine salvage and towage invoicing involving non-trade-correlated emergency wire payments and Lloyd's Open Form awards settling outside normal trade cycles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Lloyd's Standard Form of Salvage Agreement (LOF 2020) or equivalent towage contract (TOWCON/TOWHIRE); salvage security document and insurers' Letter of Undertaking; salvage master's certificate and daily towage log; port pilotage and disbursement accounts; invoice-to-wire mapping; independent maritime surveyor's statement; and job-ticket trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound offshore capital injection from private non-resident shareholders inconsistent with zero minimum capital and default exemptions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising capital subscription and documenting the share issue; bank reference for the remitting entity; source-of-wealth evidence, including three years of personal and business bank statements, asset and business background, and home-jurisdiction tax clearances; signed statutory declarations; updated share register; and IRD capital-reporting confirmations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident individual signatories residing in high-risk or non-cooperative FATF jurisdictions, or absence of a local director.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Binding dual-signatory policy requiring one NZ-resident director or licensed professional trustee; certified passport and residency evidence; police clearance certificate; professional references from lawyers and accountants; power of attorney in favour of the New Zealand corporate-services provider; executed account mandate with authorised email domain; and quarterly director attestations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections will travel from foreign equity holders or lenders into the New Zealand International Company's NZD/USD operating account at a tier-1 bank. Recommended compliant route: (i) the remitter sends a SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer from their home treasury account to the New Zealand bank's correspondent, with purpose code 'EQUI' or 'SHARECAPITAL' and narrative describing 'International Company share subscription; ISIC 5222 offshore towage and salvage'; (ii) the receiving New Zealand bank performs sanctions screening and correspondent-bank due diligence; (iii) funds are credited within one to two banking days, after which Treasury records the mandated purpose code, the remitter name, and the underlying subscription or loan agreement reference in the ERP; and (iv) for amounts exceeding NZD 100,000, board-minute resolutions and signed subscription documents are pre-positioned with the Relationship Executive to avoid post-cycle compliance holds. No invasive FX-control approval is required; however, if the inbound funds will finance the acquisition of assets constituting significant business assets or sensitive land under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, an Overseas Investment Office exemption application must be filed where applicable before settlement. All wires must be dispatched under an internal treasury counterparty list and a third-party-remitter policy to prevent stranded funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursement clearing for maritime trade and salvage operations uses the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct customer wires for supplier invoices, crew payroll, agency fees, harbour dues, and bunker fuel, with full beneficiary bank, account, and purpose-of-payment details; (2) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank cover payments where the beneficiary instruction routes through an intermediary; (3) commercial documentary letters of credit issued or confirmed by the New Zealand tier-1 bank under UCP600 and Incoterms 2020 for major equipment or subcontractor charter contracts, preferably 100% at-sight USD or deferred 90-day usance; and (4) SWIFT gpi for end-to-end traceability. For Lloyd's Standard Form Wire disbursements from escrow, including salvage security or award payments, the Treasury mandate requires a two-signature release with at least one NZ-resident signatory, a unique salvage reference comprising the IMO number and claim code, and a pre-approved counterparty whitelist; the bank executes as a regularised wire without overnight delay. Any disbursement above USD 5,000,000 should be split into two tranches on consecutive value dates to preserve liquidity buffers and satisfy balance-of-payments reporting. Physical delivery, cheques, and crypto rails are prohibited.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot (NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, EUR/USD) for operational conversion
Deliverable FX Forwards (plain vanilla, 1-24 months) as firm hedges against contracted salvage and towage receivables
FX Swaps (rollover structures) to bridge staggered disbursement dates without spot realisation
Cross-Currency Swaps (NZD/USD and AUD/USD) for long-duration capital-injection hedges
Zero-Cost Collars and vanilla over-the-counter currency options for uncertain Lloyd's Open Form award timing
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted onshore currencies, including USD/CNY long-dated NDF, USD/IDR NDF, USD/KRW NDF, and USD/PHP NDF, referenced offshore and settled in USD
Long-dated FX Forwards (up to five years, scheduled draws) aligned with project-finance and marine-asset contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the balance date; absent a designated balance date, within 20 working days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Public register default marking; failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative cancellation under s 318 of the Companies Act 1993 after notice and objection; company and directors expose themselves to penalty fines of up to NZ$10,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report (for issuers and large private companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after balance date; extension requires Registrar approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under Companies Act 1993 s 211(2) with fine up to NZ$10,000; continuous breach for large or issuer companies may trigger Financial Markets Authority enforcement and director disqualification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Audit and Certification (Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and appointed registered agent; certificate kept at the New Zealand registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at balance date; registers updated within 10 working days of any director or member change and within 20 working days of an allotment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or unavailable registers constitute an offence under s 373 of the Companies Act 1993; directors and agent may face personal liability for conversion or misrepresentation affecting towage contract liens and escrow security

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maritime New Zealand Towage and Salvage Operator Licence and Vessel Certificate Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before certificate expiry, typically 30 days prior to the anniversary of issue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Strict-liability offence for uncovered operations; fines up to NZ$50,000 per incident, port-state detention of the tug, and suspension of salvage or towage contracts for illegality

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory if the company is large under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (total assets above NZ$60m, or total revenue above NZ$30m, or 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees), if it has public accountability (issuer, licensed insurer, registered bank, or licensed non-bank deposit taker), or if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights make a written audit request; otherwise the small-company audit exemption applies
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ GAAP: Tier 1 full IFRS with NZ amendments for public accountability; Tier 2 NZ IFRS reduced-disclosure framework for large non-public entities; Tier 3 simplified accrual basis and Tier 4 cash basis for small entities; a tax-exempt International Company commonly adopts Tier 3 or, where financiers require full transparency, full IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate UBO registry; annual confirmation is achieved through the Register of Members and the registered agent's AML/CFT customer due diligence records. Each year the agent must refresh beneficial ownership data for every non-resident shareholder, screen against sanctions, minute the review, and state on the Companies Act annual return that public-register details for directors and shareholders remain current. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members immediately; a Return of Allotment is lodged with the Companies Office within 10 working days after any new share issuance.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,500 annually for a licensed corporate service provider acting as registered office and company secretary
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–12,000 for a typical small-to-mid-tier marine holding company audit; nil if the small-company exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate for a non-resident International Company on pure foreign-source deep-sea towage and salvage income derived entirely outside New Zealand territorial waters; 28% applies to any New Zealand-source income derived within territorial waters or the EEZ where the contract is performed; no statutory tax holiday applies, but a 15% R&D tax credit is available for qualifying New Zealand marine technology development.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed limit (indefinite carryforward of tax losses, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test in s IA 5 Income Tax Act 2007)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 — Company Income Tax Return, filed through Inland Revenue myIR secure e-filing portal (IRD Number required)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional tax instalments for standard balance dates)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For the standard 31 March balance date, the e-filed IR4 is due by 7 July immediately following the income year end; where a tax agent is engaged, the filing date is extended to 31 March of the following year. Terminal tax is due 7 February. Provisional tax instalments fall due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income — total assessable income from offshore towage, salvage awards and ancillary maritime services (ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488330).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-source assessable income. Deep-sea salvage awards performed outside NZ territorial waters by a non-resident owner/operator using non-NZ-flagged vessels are foreign-source and exempt; voyage apportionment must be evidenced by logs and contract place-of-performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses — crew wages, fuel, hull insurance, port dues, broker commissions and Lloyd's salvage arbitration costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses directly incurred in deriving assessable New Zealand-source income. Global fleet overheads must be apportioned consistently with OECD transfer pricing principles; no deduction is allowed for notional intra-group management charges without substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits — income tax paid to overseas jurisdictions on the same income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may attach a foreign tax credit only for foreign tax paid on income that is also assessable in New Zealand; foreign taxes on pure offshore work are not creditable in NZ and must be recovered under the relevant DTA if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after losses carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC, carry forward losses are available only if the loss year company satisfied the continuity of ownership requirement, and only against same-source NZ taxable income; exempt offshore income cannot absorb NZ losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 28% on taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply a flat 28% corporate rate; no provincial or local corporate income tax is imposed on top of national tax. A non-resident IC whose only income is foreign-source will show zero taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Terminal tax payable or refund — net of provisional tax and RWT/NRWT credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle any balance through IRD electronic payment on or before terminal tax due date; late payment triggers monthly incremental penalties and use-of-money interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Filing Penalty: initial $250 for companies with gross income under NZ$1 million, $500 otherwise, plus $50 per day for continuing default up to a 50-day cap. Late Payment Penalty: flat 1% on unpaid tax at the due date, then 4% after two months, repeating every two months up to a maximum 10% cap. A use-of-money interest charge (currently 9.13% per annum on underpayments) accrues daily on unpaid terminal and provisional tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on cash and non-cash distributions; a 15% reduced rate applies under an applicable double tax agreement where the non-resident corporate shareholder holds at least 10% of the voting power and a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) is held by the payee.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the payee must be the beneficial owner of the dividend, obtain a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence, submit the TRC together with Form IR372 to the New Zealand paying agent prior to payment, and the payer must retain the documents. Where the treaty rate has not been applied in time, a retrospective refund may be claimed through the IRD IR65A non-resident withholding tax refund process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties. Under New Zealand's comprehensive DTAs, the treaty rate for interest is commonly 10%, and for industrial/commercial royalties 5–10%, provided the TRC and beneficial-ownership requirements are met. The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) at 2% may fully replace NRWT on qualifying offshore interest paid to non-residents on registered securities, subject to lodgement of an AIL certificate with IRD.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Transfer Pricing documentation: required where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds NZ$10 million in the income year; for high-risk intra-group financing, intangible, management, or recharging arrangements, documentation is required where the relevant transactions exceed NZ$1 million. Master File and Country-by-Country Reporting apply where the multinational group's consolidated revenue is EUR 750 million or above (approximately NZ$1.3 billion).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not apply a formal ESR statute, but s BG1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) and the 'Parliamentary contemplation' core purpose test nullify arrangements that lack economic substance. An International Company claiming non-resident status and tax-exempt treatment for offshore towage must prove that central management and control, charterparty negotiation, voyage-planning decisions, and salvage arbitration authority sit physically outside New Zealand. A passport-style mail-dropped company with decision-making exercised from an Auckland office will be re-characterised as tax resident and fully taxable, with shortfall penalties attached.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately failing to disclose New Zealand-source towage/salvage income, falsifying voyage logs to mischaracterise domestic towing as offshore salvage, or shifting profits to a zero-taxed International Company without arm's length consideration, intending to defeat tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ss 143 and 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, criminal evasion is punishable by a fine up to NZ$100,000 for a body corporate, alongside a civil shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the evaded tax; the company is also liable for the unpaid primary tax plus use-of-money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knew of or were party to the evasion face imprisonment for up to 5 years and fines up to NZ$50,000, personal assessment of the shortfall under s 34 of the Tax Administration Act, disqualification under the Companies Act 1993, and a departure prohibition order preventing the director from leaving New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a letterbox entity with no physical office, no operational marine assets, no employees, no independent insurance cover, and no economic substance, solely to access a Tax-Exempt Zone classification and avoid New Zealand corporate tax on a towage/salvage business functionally managed from New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the entity as a New Zealand tax resident with worldwide income taxed at 28%; cancellation of tax benefits under the GAAR; shortfall penalties up to 100% of tax avoided (up to 150% if knowing evasion is established); suspension or revocation of maritime towage/salvage licences by Maritime New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax shortfall where they directed the arrangement, may be disqualified for up to 5 years, and may face seizing of personal assets, travel bans, and imprisonment where dishonest deception is found.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting a Lloyd's Open Form salvage award, tug hire ransom, or emergency towage payment without conducting customer due diligence, identifying beneficial owners, screening against sanctions lists, or maintaining transaction records, or structuring payments to obscure the salvage proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a body corporate faces civil penalties up to NZ$2 million per contravention, with criminal prosecutions for wilful misconduct attracting fines up to NZ$2.5 million plus seizure of the property involved in the transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are treated as 'officers' and may be personally civilly liable where the breach occurred with their express or implied authority; individual directors may also be prosecuted for money laundering offences and imprisoned for up to 7 years, and travel bans can be imposed to secure their attendance and payment of penalties.
